source_facts.problem_category: Hash maps; interleaved array storage; collision resolution; masked indexing
mechanisms: Owns transient Object[] table and occupied count; adjacent slots hold each key and value.
Null keys and collision buckets use special sentinel objects.
Collision buckets use additional Object[] arrays of consecutive key/value pairs instead of stored Entry nodes.
Capacity selection uses power-of-two growth; hash mixing and a bit mask choose an even key-slot index.
Insertion writes key/value slots directly and rehashes when occupied exceeds maxSize.
source_facts.entry_storage_assessment: Strong candidate for no stored Entry nodes; the class documentation explicitly describes array collision storage. Inspection is targeted, not a proof of every internal operation.
source_facts.selection_rationale: Reuse the existing array map and collision representation before designing another generic hash table.
observable_limits: Additional collision arrays remain part of the storage layout; this is not a single flat global array.
No allocation measurement, differential corpus, worst-case guarantee or speed comparison was executed.
Null handling, equality direction, iterator behavior, serialization, resizing and subclass hooks need separate contract qualification before adaptation.

source_facts.problem_category: Dynamic arrays; contiguous range compaction; direct indexed traversal
mechanisms: Owns protected int size and transient T[] items.
Separate shared empty-array sentinels distinguish default construction from explicit zero capacity.
Range deletion shifts a suffix using System.arraycopy and clears/reset the vacated end.
Sorting, reversal and internal traversal directly use the owned array.
Wrap-copy and backing-array factory variants expose distinct copy-versus-alias behavior.
source_facts.entry_storage_assessment: Array-owned list candidate; no map-entry storage is required by the inspected list representation.
source_facts.selection_rationale: Existing dynamic-array ownership and bulk operations fit M3 array/index refinement.
observable_limits: FastList explicitly documents lack of concurrent-modification exceptions. Replacing it with an ordinary fail-fast list would change behavior.
Factory array aliasing, copy/clone semantics and subclass-visible storage must be preserved.
The excerpts do not qualify all growth, overflow or serialization paths; no tests or benchmarks were executed.

source_facts.problem_category: Sorted maps; range views; ordering and copy contracts
mechanisms: Package is relocated to com.m3.collections.eclipse.impl.map.sorted.mutable.
Backing field remains private java.util.TreeMap<K,V> treeMap.
The six inspected constructors allocate JDK TreeMap instances; comparator-plus-map construction creates a TreeMap then calls putAll.
source_facts.entry_storage_assessment: Current owner still delegates storage to the JDK node-backed TreeMap; relocation alone is not array conversion.
source_facts.selection_rationale: Use the existing public and behavioral surface as donor contract while replacing backing storage with separately qualified arrays/indexes.
observable_limits: This is a current public-fork source observation, not a review of any unpublished helper.
No assertion of full TreeSortedMap API implementation, serialization compatibility or whole-repository conversion follows from these excerpts.

source_facts.problem_category: Case-insensitive maps; insertion order; locale normalization; dual indexing
mechanisms: LinkedHashMap<String,V> owns ordered, original-case keys and values.
HashMap<String,String> indexes normalized strings to their original-case keys.
Lookup uses locale-based normalization; class documentation excludes null keys.
Changing the casing of an existing key can remove the old original-case mapping before inserting the replacement.
An overridable eldest-entry removal hook coordinates removal from both indexes.
source_facts.entry_storage_assessment: Current implementation uses JDK HashMap/LinkedHashMap storage; not a no-stored-entry implementation.
source_facts.selection_rationale: Reuse case preservation, ordering, locale and dual-index consistency rules while independently qualifying M3 storage.
observable_limits: Replacement casing/order, null values, locale edge cases, protected hooks and live views require differential proof.
No claim that an M3 version already preserves every Spring behavior; no tests or benchmarks executed.

source_facts.problem_category: Multimaps; list-valued mappings; shallow and deep copying; alias ownership
mechanisms: Extends MultiValueMapAdapter and supplies a LinkedHashMap backing map.
Value-holding lists use ArrayList.
Copy construction and clone reuse existing list objects.
deepCopy creates an independent ArrayList per mapping.
source_facts.entry_storage_assessment: Lists are dynamic arrays, but the backing LinkedHashMap remains node-backed.
source_facts.selection_rationale: Retain shallow/deep-copy alias behavior and ordered multimap API when replacing map storage.
observable_limits: Blind flattening of all values would lose required list sharing and externally supplied list behavior.
No MultiValueMapAdapter implementation closure, tests or performance measured in this audit.

source_facts.problem_category: Concurrent reference maps; segment locking; reference queues; masked indexing; purge and resize
mechanisms: Each segment extends ReentrantLock and owns a volatile Reference<K,V>[] array plus an AtomicInteger count.
Hash masking selects slots using hash & (references.length - 1).
Mutation allocates a stored Entry and creates a Reference linked to the prior bucket head.
Lookup and restructuring traverse Reference.getNext chains.
Reference-queue polling drives purging; restructuring can double the array and rebuild reference chains under the segment lock.
source_facts.entry_storage_assessment: Arrays and masks coexist with stored Entry objects and linked Reference chains; direct storage import does not satisfy the requested no-entry invariant.
source_facts.selection_rationale: Inventory segmented lifecycle and purge timing as a possible donor; replace node/referent ownership only with dedicated GC and concurrency qualification.
observable_limits: No weak/soft-reference liveness, concurrent linearizability or garbage-collection proof was executed.
Required reference wrappers and stored map entries are distinct concerns; this audit does not admit a replacement representation.
Selected excerpt excludes file header and full public API.
